verifications.claim: NASA is scheduled to launch the Artemis II mission on Wednesday, April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'no earlier than 6:24 p.m. EDT, Wednesday, April 1, launch teams at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R4: 'At 6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday, four astronauts are scheduled to lift off from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center'; R7: 'targeted launch time of 6:24 p.m. on Wednesday, April 1'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state the exact date, time, and location matching the claim.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will send four astronauts—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen—on a 10-day trip around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen on an approximately 10-day journey around the Moon'; R2: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, as well as Jeremy Hansen... will set off to orbit the Moon on a 10-day mission'; R4: 'four astronauts... Reid Wiseman, Christina Koch and Victor Glover and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen... 10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names and 10-day lunar trip directly supported across references.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission marks the first crewed lunar flight since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'For the first time since 1972, NASA is sending humans back on a path toward the Moon'; R3: 'first crew to head for the moon since the Apollo 17 flight... more than 50 years ago'; R4: 'first people to launch toward the moon since the Apollo 17 mission in 1972'
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly state it is the first crewed mission to the Moon vicinity since 1972 (Apollo 17).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will launch aboard the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'ready the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and Orion spacecraft'; R2: 'Launching aboard the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'; R3: 'first crewed flight atop NASA's Space Launch System rocket'; R4: 'NASA’s giant Space Launch System moon rocket'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant references confirm SLS rocket launches the crew.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will launch aboard the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'SLS... rocket and Orion spacecraft for the crew’s journey'; R2: 'first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft'; R3: 'first piloted flight of an Orion deep space crew capsule'; R4: 'Orion capsule carry into space'; R7: 'first crewed launch of NASA’s SLS... rocket and Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: References consistently state the crew launches in Orion atop SLS.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a test flight to verify systems for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'verify modern human capabilities in deep space and pave the way for long-term exploration... on the lunar surface'; R3: 'test mission... put the crew ship... through its paces... Big step toward a future moon landing'; R4: 'test mission... step toward a landing in 2028'
verifications.reasoning: Described as test mission paving way for landings, but not precisely 'verify systems for future lunar landings'; broader terms used.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will not land on the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'orbit the Moon'; R3: 'will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit... flying around the leading edge of the moon'; R4: 'They will not land on the lunar surface'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit statements confirm no landing on the Moon.
